title: Tweet Counts By Frequency
statement:
Design a small tweet counter that groups recorded tweet times into fixed-size frequency buckets.

Contract
- `recordTweet(tweetName, time)` records one occurrence for a non-null name at a non-negative second.
- `getTweetCountsPerFrequency(freq, tweetName, startTime, endTime)` supports `minute`, `hour`, and `day`, using bucket sizes 60, 3600, and 86400 seconds.
- The query range is inclusive. Return one count for each bucket starting at `startTime`, with the final bucket ending at `endTime` if the range is partial.
- Unknown tweet names return zero-filled buckets. Results are ordered from earliest bucket to latest.

Examples
after `recordTweet("a", 0), recordTweet("a", 60)`, `getTweetCountsPerFrequency("minute", "a", 0, 60)` => `[1, 1]`
after `recordTweet("a", 10), recordTweet("a", 70)`, hourly query from 0 to 3599 => `[2]`
querying an unseen tweet by minute from 0 to 120 => `[0, 0, 0]`

examples.input: after `recordTweet("a", 10), recordTweet("a", 70)`, hourly query from 0 to 3599
querying an unseen tweet by minute from 0 to 120

hints: Convert the frequency word into a bucket size in seconds.
For each recorded time in the inclusive query range, compute `(time - startTime) / bucketSize`.
A sorted map per tweet lets each query scan only records inside the requested range. Intended complexity: O(n + b) time for n matching recorded seconds and b returned buckets.
inputSyntax: Input: semicolon-separated operations record <name> <time> and query <freq> <name> <start> <end>, for example: record a 0; record a 60; query minute a 0 60
sampleInput: record a 0; record a 60; query minute a 0 60
